answer: A staking bond tied to verified work creates a cost ridge every fake identity must climb: each agent locks collateral that is slashed on fraud, so spawning thousands of sock puppets multiplies the attacker's locked capital instead of their influence. Reputation then grows only through a slow spiral of completed, attested jobs, and a newcomer cannot buy history — the wharf where trust docks admits only agents whose past deliveries check out, making a Sybil flood expensive and slow.
